title: Sohila close
hook: five hymns to sleep on: praise, one sun, the sky's aarti, the city, now

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Rehat Maryada; your line was going home. Today we close Kirtan Sohila.

Every night in a gurdwara there's a quiet moment most visitors never see. The evening singing ends. The Guru Granth Sahib, open since dawn, is closed, wrapped in cloth, and carried with care to its resting room, often lifted on someone's head while the sangat stands. The ceremony is called sukhasan, the position of rest. And as the scripture goes to rest, the words in the air are Sohila. Two weeks ago we opened these five hymns. Tonight, the whole of it.
screen: `THE SCRIPTURE IS CLOSED.` → `SUKHASAN: THE POSITION OF REST.` → `THE WORDS IN THE AIR: SOHILA.`

segments.voice: Here are the five, the way you might remember them lying in the dark. One, Guru Nanak: the house of praise. Jai ghar keerat: in the house where the Creator's praise is spoken and reflected on, sing. And the wedding at its end: the date written, friends pouring oil at the door, the bride called. Two, Guru Nanak: six schools, six teachers, six teachings, one Guru of gurus in many forms; many seasons, one sun. Three, Guru Nanak: the sky's aarti. Gagan mai thaal: the sky the platter, sun and moon the lamps, the stars the pearls, the wind the fan, the forests the flowers. Four, Guru Ram Das: the city. Kaam karodh: desire and anger crowd the body's streets, the thorn of ego pricks with every step, and meeting the holy breaks them up. Five, Guru Arjan: now. Karau benantee: listen, friends, life runs down day and night; this is the time to serve; make me the dust of the holy's feet. Look at the movement. A doorway, the calendar, the sky, back inside the body, then a friend leaning close. Praise, unity, wonder, honesty, urgency. And then sleep. That's the shape Sikhs lie down inside every night, and the same shape sung when a life is done: a whole evening, and a whole life, held between praise at the beginning and humility at the end.
screen: `ONE: THE HOUSE OF PRAISE.` · `TWO AND THREE: ONE SUN, THE SKY'S AARTI.` · `FOUR: THE CITY OF THIEVES.` · `FIVE: NOW IS THE TIME.` · then, large: `SLEEP IN PRAISE.`

segments.voice: Walk through the five in your mind, the house, the sun, the sky, the city, the friend, and give each one a breath. On the last breath, picture the day being wrapped and laid to rest, like the scripture at sukhasan. If you pray, say Waheguru once.
Sukhasan, the position of rest: as the Guru Granth Sahib is put to rest each night, Sohila is sung, five hymns by three Gurus said at bedtime and at the end of a life.
Your line: sleep in praise. Praise first, humility last, and rest in between. Two weeks of Sohila, done.

howItsDone: Sikhs read or listen to Kirtan Sohila every night before sleep, and in gurdwaras it is recited as the Guru Granth Sahib is closed and carried to rest in the sukhasan ceremony.
